s: What was the administrative unit of the Vijayanagara Empire?
x: A military governor called Nayaka was given Amarams for the salaries and army expenses; this is called the Amara Nayankara system.

s: The biggest administrative unit in the Vijayanagara Empire was
x: The Rajya/Mandala (province) was the largest unit of Vijayanagara provincial administration, above Nadu, Sthala and Grama, so Mandalam is correct.

s: Who headed a Nadu or Seema in Vijayanagara provincial administration?
x: A Nadu was under the Nadagauda and Parupatyagar; a Rajya under a prince or Durgadhipati, a Sthala under the Reddi/Gauda/Sthalakaranam and a village under the Ayagars.

s: Which of the following statements about Vijayanagara provincial governors is correct?
o: They could not keep their own armies
They held office for life without transfer
x: Governors could mint coins, levy taxes and keep armies, but they were frequently transferred.

s: What title did the Sangama princes who governed Vijayanagara provinces hold?
x: Princes governing a Rajya or Mandala under the Sangamas were titled Odeyar.

s: Before 1485, Saluva Narasimha was the governor of which Andhra rajya?
x: Saluva Narasimha governed Chandragiri before 1485; it later became a capital.

s: Which Andhra rajya became the new headquarters of Tirumala after Talikota?
x: After Talikota, Penukonda became Tirumala's new headquarters.

s: About how many rajyams were there under Achyutaraya?
x: There were about 17 rajyams under Achyutaraya.

s: Which officer of the nadu (sima) collected revenue and maintained forts in the Vijayanagara empire?
x: The Parupatyagar was the nadu/sima officer who collected revenue and maintained the forts.

s: Which was the most important Andhra rajya of the Vijayanagara empire, covering the Paka and Muliki districts (Nellore, Kadapa)?
x: Udayagiri was the most important Andhra rajya and was governed by royal princes under the first dynasty.

s: The Nayakas in the Vijayanagar empire were
o: Priests of large and powerful temples.
x: Nayakas (Amaranayakas) were military chiefs who held land (amaram) in lieu of salary, and administered it, so they were military chiefs controlling territories, not ministers, priests or ordinary cavalry.

s: What was the land assigned by the Vijayanagara king to military chiefs in lieu of cash salaries called?
x: Amaram was land granted to military chiefs, who were known as Amaranayakas, Nayaks, Palaiyagars or Poligars. The grant substituted for direct cash payment to the chiefs.

s: What title did the Vijayanagara amaranayakas hold?
x: Amaranayakas held the title Mahamandaleshwara and had more autonomy than the Durgadannayakas.

s: At which festival did Vijayanagara amaranayakas attend court with gifts?
x: Amaranayakas paid tribute, kept troops, horses and elephants, and attended court at Mahanavami with gifts.

s: What was the tribute paid by the Vijayanagara amaranayakas to the king called?
x: Amaranayakas paid tribute called Kappam and kept troops, horses and elephants for the king.

s: What was the principal political outcome of the Vijayanagara Amara-Nayankara system after 1565?
o: The replacement of Nayakas by hereditary village accountants
The conversion of all amarams into Mughal jagirs
The complete abolition of regional chieftaincies
The emergence of semi-independent and later independent Nayaka states such as Madurai, Tanjore and Keladi
x: After 1565, semi-independent Nayaka kingdoms emerged and some became independent, including those of Madurai, Tanjore and Keladi.

s: Which of the following pairs (system – characteristic) is correctly matched?
o: Vijayanagara Amara-Nayankara – Amaram fiefs and about 200 Nayakas
Vijayanagara Amara-Nayankara – Numerical zat and sawar ranks
Mughal Mansabdari – Mandalams and forts held by 75 or 77 Nayakas
Kakatiya Nayankara – Amaram fiefs and about 200 Nayakas
x: The Vijayanagara system involved amaram fiefs and about 200 Nayakas. The Kakatiya system had 75 or 77 Nayakas holding mandalams and forts, and Mughal mansabdars held zat and sawar ranks.

s: Who is identified as the originator of the Kakatiya Nayankara system?
x: Prataparudra II is identified as the originator of the Kakatiya Nayankara system. The Vijayanagara Amara-Nayankara system grew out of the Kakatiya system.

s: About how many nayakas held amarams under the Vijayanagara amara-nayankara system?
x: Vijayanagara had about 200 nayakas, against the Kakatiyas' 75 or 77.

s: The Kakatiya nayankara system had how many nayakas?
x: The Kakatiya system had 75 or 77 nayakas holding mandalams and forts; Vijayanagara had about 200.

s: Who were polygars of South India?
x: Palegars (Poligars) were the amara-nayakas who administered territories and held military obligations, so they were territorial administrative and military governors, not ordinary zamindars (they were only forerunners of zamindars).

s: From whom did the Palegars or Poligars primarily originate?
x: The Amara-nayakas became the Palegars or Poligars when central authority weakened after the Battle of Talikota.

s: The Palegars (Poligars), who became hereditary local rulers after Talikota, are regarded as the forerunners of whom?
x: The Palegars are regarded as forerunners of the zamindars; Ryotwari was introduced by Munro after suppressing them.

s: Which system did Thomas Munro introduce after suppressing the poligars of Rayalaseema?
x: Munro, with military officer Campbell, suppressed the poligars and then brought in the Ryotwari system.

s: Which British officer, assisted by Campbell, crushed the Palegars of Rayalaseema?
x: Thomas Munro, with his officer Campbell, crushed the Palegars and then introduced the Ryotwari system.

s: What was the village headman called in the Vijayanagara Empire?
x: Officers called Reddy/Karanam/Gowda headed the stala (village group); the Parupatyagar headed the Sima.

s: How many Ayagars traditionally ran each village under the Ayagar system?
x: Each village was administered by 12 hereditary Ayagars. They included officials, artisans and service providers.

s: How were the Ayagars generally paid?
o: A fixed share of customs duties alone
Tax-free Manyam lands and a share of the harvest called Mera
Regular cash salaries from the royal treasury only
x: Ayagars received tax-free Manyam lands, also called Mirasi, Bhattu Vrutti or Jatikattu Manyalu, along with a share of the harvest called Mera. They were not paid regular cash salaries.

s: Which of the following pairs (Ayagar – function) is correctly matched?
x: The Talari was the village watchman. The Karanam was the accountant, the Reddi the village head and the Purohita the priest.

s: Who was the 'Kase' among the village artisans of the Vijayanagara period?
x: Kase was the mason or house-builder; Vadrangi was the carpenter, Kummari the potter and Chakali the washerman.

s: Who collected the grain gifts called 'Merulu' in Vijayanagara villages?
x: The Talari (watchman) collected Merulu; Mera was the Ayagars' harvest share.

s: Which village officer kept the accounts and land and crop registers in Vijayanagara villages?
x: The Karanam kept accounts, land and crop registers and temple accounts; the Reddi was the village head.

s: Who supervised forced labour (vetti) in a Vijayanagara village?
x: The Begari supervised vetti (forced labour).

s: What was the village head called Reddi in Andhra known as in Karnataka?
x: The Reddi was the village head and revenue collector of Andhra; in Karnataka he was the Gauda.

s: What was the chief characteristics of financial system of Vijayanagara Empire?
x: Land revenue (share of produce, usually 1/6, and higher on fertile land) was the mainstay of Vijayanagara finance, so Land Revenue is correct.

s: The Vijayanagar King who totally withdrew the marriage tax was:

s: What is "Meruka" a tax on?
x:
Meruka was a commercial tax levied on the sale and purchase of goods during the Reddy period. Trade and commerce formed an important source of state revenue, and taxes like Meruka were imposed on market transactions carried out by merchants. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).

• Meruka – Tax on Sale and Purchase

s: Vijayanagara king who completely abolished marriage tax?
x: According to Paes and Nuniz, Sri Krishnadevaraya abolished the Kalyana Kanike (marriage tax). Sadashivaraya abolished the Mangali (barber) tax.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to land classification is correctly matched?
x: Bagayati denoted garden land. Nanja was wet land, Punja was dry land and Banjara was waste land.

s: What did Neerarambamu or Magani denote in the Andhra terminology of Vijayanagara revenue administration?
o: Garden land assessed through market tolls
x: Neerarambamu, also called Magani, was irrigated land and was generally taxed in grain at higher rates.

s: How were the rights to collect market or santhalu taxes generally given in the Vijayanagara Empire?
o: Assigned permanently to village assemblies without payment
x: The right to collect market taxes was auctioned to Sunkandarlu.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Putrodaya kanuka — Sale and purchase of goods
x: Putrodaya kanuka was a tax on the birth of a son. Sale and purchase of goods was taxed through Meruka.

s: Which of the following statements regarding Siddhaya is correct?
o: It was exclusively a military title of the commander-in-chief.
It denoted a fixed levy, with varieties connected with occupations such as cotton ginning and toddy tapping.
It was the name of the royal treasury.
It referred only to a tax on sale and purchase of goods.
x: Siddhaya meant a fixed levy. Pinje Siddhayam was connected with cotton ginners, Eidipi Siddhayam with toddy tappers and Jati Siddhayam with castes or professions.

s: On whom was the Vijayanagara tax Navidadere levied?
x: Navidadere (Kondaju) was the barbers' tax; Maneyanna was the house tax.

s: On what was the Vijayanagara tax Maneyanna (Illari Pannu) levied?
x: Maneyanna was the house tax.

s: What was the usual share of produce collected as land revenue in Vijayanagara?
x: The usual share was 1/6; fertile land paid 1/4 or 1/3.

s: Which Vijayanagara tax was levied on the birth of a son?
x: Putrodaya Kanuka was levied on the birth of a son; Kalyana Kanika was the wedding tax.

s: Which Vijayanagara ruler totally withdrew (abolished) the marriage tax?
x: The marriage tax was totally withdrawn under Sadasiva Raya (APPSC Group 1 key); Krishnadevaraya is a frequent decoy.

s: Which tax of the Vijayanagara period was levied on sale and purchase?
x: Meruka was the tax on sale and purchase; Mera was the Ayagars' harvest share and Merulu the Talari's grain gifts.

s: What were the land-tax documents of the Vijayanagara period called?
x: Land-tax documents of the Vijayanagara period were called Adhuvanatantram.

s: Which Vijayanagara ruler first remitted the marriage tax?
x: The marriage tax was first remitted by Saluva Narasimha and later abolished under Sadasiva Raya.

s: What was the practice adopted by the Vijayanagar Kings to protect the inhabitants within a fortified area from starvation due to sieges by enemy armies?
o: Large granaries were built within the fortified area to store grains
Secret pathways were maintained to transport groceries into fortified areas
Large agricultural tracts were incorporated within the fortified area
The forts were built on hills to prevent siege by the enemy
x: Per NCERT (Themes in Indian History II, ch. 7), granaries were the ordinary measure against sieges, while the Vijayanagara rulers adopted the more elaborate strategy of enclosing agricultural tracts within the fortified area.

s: Who headed the Siddha (standing) army of Vijayanagara?
x: The standing army was under the Dalavayi; Durga Dannayakas commanded forts.

s: Who was the first Vijayanagara king to use cannon?
x: Bukka I was the first Vijayanagara king to use cannon; firearms were associated with Turkish and Portuguese experts.

s: Through which ports did Vijayanagara mainly import Arabian and Persian horses?
x: Horses came via the west-coast ports Goa, Honnavar and Bhatkal; Portuguese and Arab merchants ran the trade.

s: Who introduced the Samugaris, or gunmen, into the Vijayanagara military system?
x: Saluva Narasimha introduced the Samugaris, or gunmen. Bukka I is associated with the first use of cannon by a Vijayanagara king.

s: What were the four types of forts in the Vijayanagara period?
x: The four types of forts were Giri (hill), Sthala (land), Jala (water) and Vana (forest) forts.

s: How often was the Siddha (standing) army of Vijayanagara paid?
x: The standing army was paid every four months.

s: Under whom were the forts placed in the Vijayanagara period?
x: The four kinds of forts were under Durga Dannayakas.

s: During the ancient and medieval days, Pradvivaka was an adviser to the king in:
x: Judiciary Pradvivaka was an adviser attached to the judiciary in ancient and medieval administrative systems. The post assisted the king or chief judge in adjudicating disputes and interpreting legal texts. Such officials formed part of the judicial apparatus described in inscriptions and legal literature.

s: Which of the following scriptures was considered authoritative in the administration of justice during the Vijayanagara period?
x: Parasara Madhaveeyam (Madhavacharya's commentary on Parasara Smriti) was the authoritative legal text in Vijayanagara.

s: Police rights were sometimes sold in the Vijayanagara Empire. What was this called?
x: Under the Padikaval system, police rights were sold to individuals in the Vijayanagara Empire.

s: In ancient medieval times Pradvivaka was the advisor to the king in this department?
x:
The Pradvivaka (Pradvivaka or Pradvivakudu) was the chief judicial adviser to the king in ancient and medieval Indian administration. He assisted the ruler in legal matters, interpreted Dharmashastra, advised on judicial decisions and supervised the administration of justice. His position was equivalent to that of a chief judge or legal expert in the royal court. Several ancient legal texts refer to the office of the Pradvivaka as an important component of judicial administration. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Pradvivaka – Chief Judicial Adviser
• Department – Judiciary

s: Through which work did the Vijayanagara judicial system follow the Yajnavalkya and Parashara Smritis?
x: The Yajnavalkya and Parashara Smritis were followed through Madhavacharya’s Parashara Madhaviyam.

s: What did Himsodbhava and Dhanodbhava respectively refer to in the Vijayanagara judicial system?
x: Himsodbhava referred to criminal cases, whereas Dhanodbhava referred to civil cases.

s: What was the punishment for theft in the Vijayanagara period?
x: Theft was punished by mutilation and treason by death; Brahmins received life imprisonment instead of death.

s: Who policed the village under the Vijayanagara Kavali system?
x: The Talari policed the village, the Peta Kavalidaru the towns and the Kavali Daru the Sthala.

s: What punishment did a Brahmin guilty of a crime punishable by death receive in the Vijayanagara period?
x: Brahmins got life imprisonment instead of death.

s: Who policed the Sthala level under the Kavali system?
x: Talari policed the village, Kavali Daru the sthala and Peta Kavalidaru the towns.

The head of the village police
The officer in charge of the treasury
The commander of the hill forts
